findings.summary: Todo checklist understates actual progress: several steps are marked unchecked even though the corresponding work already exists in the repo.
findings.evidence: docs/tasks/active/20260724-notes-empty-bullet-setext-todo.md lines with '- [ ] Add packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts', '- [ ] Wire it into preview.ts', '- [ ] Unit tests in preview.test.ts', '- [ ] Note the deviation in docs/design/notes/notes.md' are all unchecked, but packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts exists, is imported in preview.ts, preview.test.ts references the setext/empty-bullet behavior, and docs/design/notes/notes.md already has a '#### Empty nested bullet vs setext heading — shipped (issue #517)' section documenting the deviation.

findings.summary: The list-interrupt relaxation applies to `*` and `+` bullets too, while the lheading half only relaxes `-`; this silently changes rendering of `foo\n*` / `foo\n+` beyond the documented `-`-only deviation
findings.evidence:
`isEmptyBulletLine` (line 39) accepts DASH, `*` (0x2a) and `+` (0x2b), and `wrappedList` returns `true` (terminate paragraph) for any of them. Upstream markdown-it refuses to let an *empty* bullet of any marker interrupt a paragraph, so `foo\n*` previously rendered as lazy paragraph text `foo
*`; it now renders as a paragraph plus an empty `
`. Both the design doc (docs/design/notes/notes.md:293-299) and the task doc scope the deviation to a "lone single `-`", and no test covers `*`/`+`. Asymmetric with `lheadingRule`, which only special-cases DASH.

findings.summary: Replacement lheading uses an ASCII-only trim where upstream uses String.prototype.trim(), so setext heading content keeps leading/trailing Unicode whitespace
findings.evidence: Line 134 does `asciiTrim(state.getLines(...))` with ASCII_TRIM_RE = /^[\x09-\x0d\x20]+|.../g, but markdown-it 14's rules_block/lheading.mjs ends with `state.getLines(startLine, nextLine, state.blkIndent, false).trim()` — JS `.trim()` also strips U+00A0, U+2028, U+3000, etc. A heading like ` Heading \n===` therefore renders with the NBSP retained, diverging from the paragraph rule (which still uses `.trim()`) and from the rest of the document. The comment claiming markdown-it has its own `asciiTrim` used here appears inaccurate for the lheading rule.

findings.summary: Single-dash setext H2 (`Heading\n-`) no longer renders as a heading anywhere in a note — a rendering regression for previously valid documents (deliberate, but untested and unbounded)
findings.evidence: `const isLoneDash = marker === DASH && runLength === 1;` at line 105 rejects the underline globally, not only inside list contexts. Existing notes written as `Title\n-` now render as a paragraph followed by a stray empty bullet list. The task doc lists a "top-level lone dash" test (docs/tasks/active/20260724-notes-empty-bullet-setext-todo.md:62) but preview.test.ts adds none, so the blast radius of the deviation is unasserted. Deliberate per docs/design/notes/notes.md:293, flagged only because the collateral case is broader than the issue and uncovered.

findings.summary: Single-dash setext heading (`Heading\n-`) — the exact input class the lheading rewrite disqualifies — has no test
findings.evidence:
The new `lheadingRule` adds `isLoneDash` (list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:105) so a lone `-` never produces a setext `

`. That is a real, user-visible behavior change for the ordinary top-level document `Heading\n-`, which CommonMark renders as `

Heading

` and now renders as a paragraph + empty list. The only setext test is `preview.render('Heading\n---')` (preview.test.ts:184), which uses a multi-dash underline and therefore never reaches the new guard. I grepped every `preview.render('` fixture in packages/notes (13 total, listed above) and searched the repo for `lheading|setext|listEmptyBullet` — no test anywhere feeds a lone `-` underline at top level. So the change's most consequential deviation ships uncovered in either direction (neither the new nor the old behavior is pinned).

findings.summary: The whole lheading rule was re-implemented but only one heading shape is tested
findings.evidence: lheadingRule is a hand-copied reimplementation of upstream markdown-it's rule, including the `=`-underline branch, the >3-space indent guards, the blockquote `sCount < 0` quirk, the paragraph terminator loop and a locally re-created `asciiTrim`. The only heading assertion is `Heading\n---` (preview.test.ts:184). No test covers `Heading\n===` (level-1 path, `level = 1`), a heading inside a blockquote, or content trimming, so a transcription error in any of those branches passes CI silently.

findings.summary: The `alt: ['paragraph','reference','blockquote']` restoration is called out as a regression risk yet has no test
findings.evidence: The comment at list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:195-199 says that without restoring the alt chain the `list` rule 'stops terminating' paragraphs/references/blockquotes. No new test feeds a paragraph interrupted by a normal list (`text\n- item`), a link reference definition followed by a list, or a list inside a blockquote. The nearest test, 'leaves a non-empty nested list unchanged' (preview.test.ts:189), starts with a list, so it never exercises paragraph interruption. If the alt array were dropped or wrong, the suite would stay green.

findings.summary: Two of the five new tests pass identically on stock markdown-it and pin no new behavior
findings.evidence: 'still renders the blank-line workaround correctly' (line 175) and 'leaves a non-empty nested list unchanged' (line 189) both render inputs that unmodified markdown-it already handles the asserted way, so they cannot distinguish the plugin being installed from it being absent. They are legitimate regression guards, but they inflate the apparent coverage of the new rule; only lines 153-173 actually exercise the fix.

Approach couples notes to markdown-it internals: an ~80-line verbatim fork of upstream `lheading` plus a private `__rules__` read
findings.evidence: `lheadingRule` is a copy of markdown-it 14.x `rules_block/lheading.mjs` with one added guard, `asciiTrim` re-implements a private upstream helper, and `getRuleFn` reads `md.block.ruler.__rules__` (explicitly documented as private, line 205-213). packages/notes/package.json pins `markdown-it: ^14.1.0`, so a semver-minor upstream change to `lheading` silently diverges from the fork with no test that would notice. A lighter-touch alternative (a block rule registered `before('lheading')`/`before('list')` that handles only the empty-bullet line, as `details-plugin.ts` already does with `md.block.ruler.before(...)`) would avoid both the fork and the private-API read.

findings.summary: Small duplication with details-plugin.ts: the `StateBlock` type derivation and its explanatory comment are copy-pasted
findings.evidence: `type StateBlock = InstanceType<MarkdownIt['block']['State']>;` and the accompanying `export =` comment appear verbatim in both packages/notes/src/view/details-plugin.ts:3-7 and this new file. A tiny shared `markdown-it-types.ts` (or the existing packages/notes/src/markdown-it-plugins.d.ts) would hold it once.

samples.summary: `getRuleFn` reads markdown-it's private `__rules__` and throws at module-import time; any internal rename in a permitted `^14` minor upgrade takes down the entire notes preview module
samples.evidence: `getRuleFn` casts `md.block.ruler` to `{ __rules__: ... }` and `throw new Error('markdown-it block rule not found: list')` if the shape changes (line 212). `listEmptyBulletPlugin` is invoked at module top level via `md.use(...)` in preview.ts:48, so the throw happens during module evaluation, not at render time — the whole `preview.ts` module (and anything importing NotePreview) fails to load rather than degrading to the old rendering. packages/notes/package.json pins `markdown-it: ^14.1.0`, so a minor bump can change internals without a lockfile-visible major. A safer form is to capture the rule via a temporary `md.block.ruler.at`/`before` dance or to keep a reference to the imported default rule.

verdict.reason: The code exists exactly as quoted (list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:207-214 reads private `__rules__` and throws at :212; preview.ts:48 invokes it at module scope), but it is not a blocking correctness defect. The throw is unreachable with the dependency actually installed: pnpm-lock.yaml:649-651 resolves markdown-it to 14.3.0 for packages/notes, whose Ruler keeps entries in `__rules__` and always registers the `list` rule in the default preset (presets only flip `enabled`). preview.test.ts:153-191 renders markdown through this plugin, which can only pass if preview.ts evaluated and getRuleFn returned. The risk described is a speculative future upstream rename under the `^14` range — dependency-coupling/robustness (design lens), not a wrong condition, boundary error, missing null guard, or async mistake on any reachable path. Additionally, the finding's own suggested remedy does not change the failure mode: line 175 already calls `md.block.ruler.at('lheading', ...)`, and markdown-it's `Ruler.at` throws `Parser rule not found` for a missing name, so the same hypothetical rename would abort module load before getRuleFn is reached; there is no graceful-degradation behavior being lost. No unguarded caller exists either — `listEmptyBulletPlugin` has exactly one call site (preview.ts:48).

verdict.reason:
The `isLoneDash` guard at list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:105-107 is unconditional on nesting context, so a top-level `Heading -` — which CommonMark/upstream markdown-it renders as `

Heading

` — now renders as a paragraph plus an empty list. That is a distinct, user-visible behavior change from the rewritten `lheading` rule. The only setext fixture in the suite is `preview.render('Heading ---')` (preview.test.ts:184), whose three-dash underline gives runLength === 3, so `isLoneDash` is false and the new guard is never reached; the other plugin tests all use nested/indented empty bullets (`- 1 -`, `- 1 - `, `- 1 - `, `- 1 - 2`). I searched wider than the reviewer: repo-wide greps for the literal lone-dash underline shapes returned only preview.test.ts:184 and a docs line; a grep for `NotePreview|preview.render|renderMarkdown` showed preview.test.ts is the only test file that renders markdown at all; no test file anywhere imports/constructs markdown-it directly (grep for `markdown-it|MarkdownIt` over all *.test/*.spec files: no files found), so there is no lower-level rule test; and there is no fixture corpus or CommonMark spec suite under packages/notes (the only `commonmark` hit is a prose comment in the plugin). No counterexample exists — the top-level lone-dash behavior ships uncovered in either direction.

samples.summary: Fix is broader than the issue: ALL single-dash setext H2s are disabled, not just the nested-bullet case
samples.evidence: `const isLoneDash = marker === DASH && runLength === 1;` unconditionally disqualifies a lone `-` underline anywhere in the document, plus the wrapped `list` rule lets any empty bullet interrupt any paragraph. Issue #517 only describes an *indented, nested* empty bullet under a list item, but this change also converts the valid top-level document `Title\n-` (a legal CommonMark setext H2) into a paragraph followed by an empty list. The design doc (docs/design/notes/notes.md:297) glosses this as "ordinary setext headings still render", which is only true for multi-dash/`=` forms. Consider scoping the deviation to the case where the dash line is more indented than / inside a list (state.listIndent / blkIndent context) so unrelated documents keep CommonMark behavior.
